- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply downward correction of 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.0) within 5 days, model frequently underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to counteract sentiment-driven sell-off bias.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in responding to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns negative after a positive streak; delay correction by 1–2 days to avoid premature reversal.
- In low-volatility periods (e.g., 3–5 consecutive low sentiment days), model tends to underestimate; apply upward bias of 0.5–1.5% to account for mean reversion toward prior highs.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.0/1.0), model often averages out extremes; use sentiment-weighted median or trimmed mean to reduce noise-driven overfitting.
